reader_question: Where did each 2024 presidential nominee’s joint fundraising committees send what they raised?
grade_line: Documented: the committees’ reports to the Federal Election Commission
title: Kamala D. Harris’s three joint fundraising committees sent $955.9 million to 54 other committees in the 2024 cycle, and Donald J. Trump’s four sent $679.8 million to 56.
measure_line: Dollars each 2024 presidential nominee’s joint fundraising committees transferred to other committees (line 22 of their reports), 2023 to 2024 election cycle, not adjusted for inflation; a link’s width is its dollars, on one scale for both
notes: Each nominee’s bar holds every committee the Federal Election Commission designates a joint fundraising committee that paid the nominee’s campaign in the cycle: for Kamala D. Harris, the Harris Victory Fund, the Harris Action Fund and the Harris Baldwin Victory Fund; for Donald J. Trump, the Trump National Committee JFC, the Trump Save America Joint Fundraising Committee, the Trump 47 Committee and the Trump Bilirakis Victory Fund. The table gives each fund’s transfers.

A joint fundraising committee raises money for several committees at once and splits it among them by the agreement that formed it, which sets how many committees it pays; a transfer passes on money raised for the committee that gets it.

Harris’s funds paid the state party committees of the 50 states and the District of Columbia, and Trump’s those of 48 states, the District of Columbia and Guam; a committee two funds paid counts once. The download lists each with its transfers.

Drawn here are transfers, line 22 of each committee’s reports, where a joint fundraising committee reports the shares it passes on. On the same reports, Harris’s funds also paid committees drawn here $27.3 million for operating expenses (line 21B) and Trump’s $12.7 million, which the chart leaves out. Harris’s funds refunded $81,000 to two committees that had given to them, and Trump’s $4,000 to four (line 28C); the table sets the refunds apart.
alt: Two senders side by side, one bar for each nominee’s joint fundraising committees, with links to bars for the committees they transferred money to, every bar as tall and every link as wide as its dollars on one scale. Kamala D. Harris’s three funds sent $533.7 million to the Harris campaign, $240.8 million to the Democratic National Committee, $181.4 million to 51 state party committees and $38,640 to one other committee, $955.9 million in all. Donald J. Trump’s four funds sent $407.8 million to the Trump campaign, $163.8 million to the Republican National Committee, $69.9 million to 50 state party committees and $38.3 million to four other committees, $679.8 million in all.
chart_notes: The chart draws both nominees’ committees alike, in one ink, on one scale: each bar is as tall as the dollars it sent or received, and each link as wide as the dollars it carried; a link under $4 million shows as a hairline.

table.caption: Transfers by each nominee’s joint fundraising committees to other committees, 2023 to 2024 cycle, one row for each fund and kind of committee it paid, with refunds set apart; the download lists every committee
